subject: Bridge load pressure: queue growth, p99 latency spike & customer readout
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart SRE <sre@brightcart.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Bridge load pressure: queue growth, p99 latency spike & customer readout

Team —

We started seeing sustained queue growth on the "bridge" routing tier at ~08:40 PDT. p99 for generation endpoints jumped from ~1.2s to ~5.6s and queued requests are backlogging (visible in the bridge queue metric). Early evidence points to a burst of short-sequence requests that are causing KV-cache churn and preventing efficient batching. Dashboard snapshot attached. Logs archive attached for SRE triage.

Immediate asks:
- SRE: please triage root cause and advise whether we should route BrightCart traffic off the bridge tier to dedicated pools or enable the protective fallback (route->realtime-fallback) for the next hour.
- Product/Runtime (Marissa, Marcus): we need a quick decision on two short-term mitigations I can offer the customer: (1) enable a routing exception to send BrightCart to dedicated pool; (2) temporarily enable stricter ingress shaping per-key for 30m. Which is faster?
- Customer comms: I drafted a short readout (customer_readout_draft.md attached). Sam, I would like to send the readout within 30 minutes if we have a mitigation and ETA.

Context: BrightCart is in a pilot with bursty traffic patterns (large user queries multiplied by many small assistant prompts). They also have deadline-related traffic spikes today (marketing campaign).

Priority: high — this is impacting BrightCart p99 and could affect our SLA.

Irene
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart SRE <sre@brightcart.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge load pressure: queue growth, p99 latency spike & customer readout

Irene — thanks for the heads up and artifacts. We see the same signal in the runtime traces. Quick notes from triage:

- Short path: we can apply a routing exception for BrightCart to shift them to the dedicated pool within ~8–12 minutes (need Marcus to open the pool and confirm capacity).
- Slightly longer: an ingress shaping rule (per-customer soft throttling) can be deployed as a config flip that takes ~20–30 minutes to validate in canary.
- Fallback: enabling realtime-fallback to the lower-cost variant is instantaneous from control plane, but it'll increase p50 slightly and may affect token-cost accounting.

I recommend: 1) route BrightCart to dedicated pool now to arrest queue growth, 2) deploy ingress shaping in parallel and keep realtime-fallback as an emergency escape hatch.

Marcus — can you confirm dedicated pool availability for a temporary exception? If capacity is tight, suggest we carve a fractional pool focused on low-seq jobs.

I'll start prepping customer-facing language once Marcus confirms.

—Marissa
Director, Product (Runtime)
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart SRE <sre@brightcart.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge load pressure: queue growth, p99 latency spike & customer readout

Quick findings from runtime traces (initial):

- Pattern: ~70% of requests are short sequences (<= 32 tokens) but extremely high QPS; these produce small KV footprints and TTLs that cause frequent cache eviction.
- Batching inefficiency: because requests are high variance we fail to batch efficiently; per-request overhead dominates particularly on the bridge tier that shares kernels across models.
- No evidence yet of model-slow path or kernel OOMs. Memory looks stable.

Short-term mitigations (feasibility):
1) Dedicated pool routing (Marissa's suggestion) — immediate and low risk. Feature parity: same model set, but per-customer autoscaling config defaults may differ (we can keep identical model versions).
2) Ingress shaping (soft per-key token throttle) — deployable in ~25 minutes, will smooth bursts and improve batching. Risk: small number of requests may be dropped if client retries aggressively.
3) Temporary micro-cache for very-short sequences (experiment) — requires a 1–2 day engineering effort; not helpful for immediate mitigation.

Product asks / roadmap questions:
- Can we prioritize an "adaptive micro-batcher" item (tiny sequences optimization) in the next sprint? This is likely to materially reduce unit cost for customers with bursty short prompts.
- Need guidance from Product on whether to offer BrightCart a short-term dedicated pool at no charge (pilot credit) given SLA exposure.

I'll keep digging and will post another update in 15 minutes.

—Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Price <sam@brightcart.com>, BrightCart SRE <sre@brightcart.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Bridge load pressure: queue growth, p99 latency spike & customer readout

Thanks all — short status and actions.

Status:
- Marcus confirmed we have spare fractional capacity in the east-us dedicated cluster; routing exception applied at 10:50 PDT. Early signals: queue drained within ~7 minutes and p99 dropped back to ~1.4s.
- Ingress shaping config initiated at 10:58 PDT; canary looks healthy. We'll keep the shaping in place for 60 minutes and reassess.

Customer impact & billing:
- Feature parity: no functional differences; BrightCart will remain on the same model versions.
- Billing: routing to dedicated pool will count against their reserved burst capacity. Marcus — please confirm whether this triggers overage billing or if we should apply a pilot credit.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Marcus Lin: confirm billing/credit model for this temporary exception and note capacity used (ETA 30m).
- Soojin Lee & SRE: continue traces for 2 hours to ensure no recurrence; share additional findings in #bridge-incidents.
- Marissa Cole: file a short-term roadmap ticket for an "adaptive micro-batcher" and estimate effort (target: T-shirt S, spike in next sprint).
- Irene: send the readout below to Sam and his ops team once Marcus confirms billing guidance.

--- DRAFT CUSTOMER READOUT (to send to BrightCart) ---
Hi Sam / BrightCart Ops —

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary of the incident: between 08:40–10:50 PDT today we observed a traffic pattern with a very high rate of short-sequence requests which caused excessive KV-cache churn on our shared "bridge" routing tier. This resulted in increased queueing and elevated p99 latency for your requests.

What we did:
- Immediately routed BrightCart to a dedicated pool (10:50 PDT) which drained the queue and restored p99 latency to baseline within ~7 minutes.
- Deployed a temporary ingress shaping rule (10:58 PDT) to smooth short, bursty traffic while we monitor.
- Ongoing: SRE is continuing trace analysis to ensure no reoccurrence and product is evaluating a targeted optimization.

Impact and next steps:
- User-facing impact: short-lived slowdown affecting autosuggest for some users; no data loss.
- Billing: we are clarifying whether the temporary capacity will be covered under your reserved burst capacity or if a credit applies. We will confirm within 30 minutes.
- Follow-up: we will schedule a 30-minute post-incident sync with BrightCart next week to review findings, share telemetry, and propose a small runtime optimization aimed at short sequences.

Please let me know if you'd like any additional details or a written incident report.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
